---
title: "Command line"
---

nota2md has two verbs, one of them implicit. A bare `codNota` is the `build`
form, which the verb may be left out of; `download` puts the GitHub releases
the project reads on disk.

```bash
nota2md [build] <codNota> [--fecha YYYY-MM-DD] [--source {auto,dof,html,image,pdf}]
        [--instrumento SLUG] [--cache-dir DIR] [--refrescar] [--notas PATH]
        [--min-confidence N] [--keep-pages] [--keep-mineru-output] [--outdir DIR]
nota2md download {federal-laws,federal-regulations,federal-guidelines,
                  international-treaties,gazette-metadata,all} ...
```

## `build`: one legal provision

```bash
nota2md 5788357                        # no --outdir: written into nota2md's cache, path printed
nota2md 5788357 --outdir output        # the law at that reform (SCJN), else the DOF
nota2md 5788357 --source dof --outdir output    # the original source only, never the SCJN
```

### `--source`

Where to build the Markdown from. `auto` (the default) answers with the SCJN's
consolidated text of the whole law at that reform when the `scjn-leyes` release
covers the `codNota`, otherwise the DOF; `dof` skips the SCJN and takes the
original source, HTML when the note has digital text and OCR otherwise; `html`,
`image` and `pdf` force one DOF path. See [Sources](sources.qmd).

### `--instrumento`

Which law is meant, by its slug, when one decree reformed several at once. The
SCJN path refuses to guess and raises, listing the candidates, until this says.

```bash
nota2md 5793655 --instrumento lft --outdir output
```

### `--fecha`

The note's publication date. Some codes from 1999 and 2000 the DOF's website
only resolves when given alongside their own date; pass it when it is already
known.

### `--outdir`

The output directory. Omitted, the Markdown is written into nota2md's own
cache (`scjn-leyes/md/` for the SCJN path, `dof/` for every DOF path) and its
path printed, so the caller does not have to pick a directory to get a note.

### `--cache-dir`

The directory this note's own Markdown is cached under (see `nota2md.cache`);
given explicitly, it is also where the SCJN path reads the `scjn-leyes` tarball
from. Not given, nota2md's output uses `nota2md.cache.CACHE_DIR` and the SCJN
path reads `scjn.cache.CACHE_DIR`, a separate directory. `none` skips nota2md's
own cache, so the DOF path is downloaded fresh every time; it does not skip the
SCJN's cache, which is disk-first and never downloads on demand.

```bash
nota2md 5793655 --cache-dir /mnt/datos/nota2md --outdir output
nota2md 5793655 --cache-dir none --refrescar --outdir output
```

### `--refrescar`

Re-extract the SCJN path's already-cached snapshot into this note's own
Markdown cache even if one is already there. It re-downloads nothing.

### `--notas`

A saved day's legal provisions as JSON (for example from `dofjson DATE`), to
source the next note's title from instead of fetching it; image path only.
Either shape works: `get_notas()`'s per-edition dict or
`fetch_daily_legal_provisions()`'s flat list.

```bash
dofjson 2026-07-15 --outdir output          # writes 15072026-notas.json
nota2md 5793655 --source image --notas output/15072026-notas.json --outdir output
```

### `--min-confidence`

The minimum title-match confidence, between 0 and 1, before a cut boundary is
applied on the image path; below it more text is kept rather than less. The
default is 0.6.

### `--keep-pages` and `--keep-mineru-output`

`--keep-pages` also keeps the uncut, full-page OCR output as
`nota-<codNota>.full.md`. `--keep-mineru-output` also keeps mineru's own raw
output (layout and model JSON, rendered PDFs) under `nota-<codNota>_mineru/`
instead of discarding it. Both are for the image and PDF paths only.

## `download`: the releases on disk

Everything else reads from the releases the project publishes. `download`
fetches them ahead of time, each into the per-user cache directory of the
package that owns it, so a notebook, a batch run or an offline session finds
them already there.

```bash
nota2md download federal-laws              # scjn-leyes (~380 MB, 315 laws)
nota2md download federal-regulations       # scjn-reglamentos
nota2md download federal-guidelines        # scjn-lineamientos
nota2md download international-treaties    # scjn-tratados
nota2md download gazette-metadata          # notas-archivo (~59 MB, 117 assets)
nota2md download all                       # all five, each into its own cache
```

### `--slug`

On `federal-laws` and `all`: only this law's tarball, by slug, repeatable. Not
given, every law the release publishes. The reverse index always comes along,
since it is what resolves a `codNota` to a law.

```bash
nota2md download federal-laws --slug lft --slug lfca
nota2md download all --slug lfca           # narrows the scjn-leyes half only
```

### `--id`

On `federal-regulations`, `federal-guidelines` and `international-treaties`:
only this instrument's tarball, by `id_ordenamiento`, repeatable. None of these
collections has an `abrev`, so they take `--id`, never `--slug`; `all` has no
`--id`, since an id could not say which of the three collections it names.

```bash
nota2md download federal-regulations --id 4570340
nota2md download international-treaties --id 1012
```

### `--cache-dir` on `download`

The directory to write into. On the four SCJN subcommands it is an `scjn`
directory (`scjn.cache.CACHE_DIR` by default, `$SCJN_CACHE_DIR`); on
`gazette-metadata` it is a `dofjson` one (`dofjson.titulos.CACHE_DIR`). `none`
is rejected here: each subcommand exists to write a release to disk.

### `--refrescar` on `download`

Re-download assets already present instead of keeping them. Every subcommand
is idempotent otherwise: an asset already on disk is matched by file name and
never revalidated, so a second run downloads nothing. Each line of output says
how many assets were downloaded versus already cached and names the directory:

```console
$ nota2md download federal-laws --slug lfca
[1/2] indice-global.json.gz: already cached
[2/2] lfca.tgz: already cached
scjn-leyes: 2 assets in /home/user/.cache/scjn/scjn-leyes (0 downloaded, 2 already cached)
```
